--- attachment: privatelink_connection_steps.pdf (pdf, 120KB)
--- attachment: vpc_boundary_matrix.csv (csv, 12KB)

Key technical notes (summary):
- Hosting boundary: production tenant deploys to our eu-west-1 pool and customer data plane is pinned to eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 AZs only. Control plane logs are stored in the EU for customers who opt into EU-only (we have a switchable control-plane storage option).
- Egress: default behavior is zero-cross-border egress for EU-only tenants. Scheduled telemetry and billing telemetry are batched and stored within the EU. We do not route inference payloads to non-EU regions for processing.
- Private Link steps (see attached runbook): establish Private Endpoint in your VNet, share allowed FQDN/IP blocks, configure TLS mutual auth if required, set up DNS override for .redwood-inference.internal, open ports 443 outbound from your peered subnets, and validate routes to KV store for KMS (if using customer-managed keys ensure key access is restricted to EU KMS partition).
- KMS: our recommended approach for customers requiring strict separation is to use customer-managed keys via the KMS integration (keys streeted in the EU KMS partition). We can also provide an HSM-backed option on Dedicated for an additional contract amendment.

Kimberly — I left placeholders in the CSV for CAIQ mapping (network isolation controls). Once you confirm the SIG/CAIQ references we'll mark the package as ready to sign.

Proposed delivery: Hannah signs the hosting paragraph; we attach the two files and a short cover note to Alice.

-Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
